source.title: Comparing Computational Pathology Foundation Models using Representational Similarity Analysis

record.file_problem: None; the full paper, including appendix tables and figures, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures representational similarity across pathology models and reports incomplete, variable alignment; it also shows that sharing a training paradigm does not ensure greater similarity. It does not test convergence as models scale or improve in capability.
record.gate_note: The study compares model representational dissimilarity matrices (RDMs), including under alternative distance metrics, stain normalization, and a changed patch-sampling scheme. Rows for slide/disease specificity and intrinsic dimensionality are omitted because they do not measure cross-model convergence. Cited results from other studies are not included.
record.test_reason: The study directly measures incomplete cross-model alignment and tests its sensitivity to distance metric, stain normalization and sampling. These results bear on V6 and the incomplete-alignment component of V7. It does not test convergence with scale or capability.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. Under the primary Euclidean analysis, UNI2 and Virchow2 have the lowest average similarities and Prov-GigaPath the highest. Shared pretraining paradigm does not guarantee greater similarity, and the causes remain unclear. Sampling and stain normalization largely preserve similarity structure. Changing the RDM metric produces quantitative changes, including raising UNI2's average to 0.527, so its low-average position is metric-dependent. The authors do not establish scaling convergence, causal explanations of alignment or interchangeability.
record.recipe_differences: Uses RSA: Euclidean distances among patch embeddings, followed by Spearman correlation between model RDMs. It does not test an explicit scale or capability progression.
record.method_sensitivity: The choice of RDM distance metric changed quantitative similarity values (correlation of original and alternative full similarity sets: 0.84). Stain normalization changed mean model similarities but was described as having little effect on the RDM correlation structure. Altered patch sampling produced highly similar results; Pearson correlation between original and changed model-similarity values was 0.997.
record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 297, Machine Learning for Health (ML4H) 2025
record.problems: All studied cancer cohorts came from TCGA, so generalization to other institutions and staining or scanner settings is untested. RSA sample size is constrained by quadratic memory demand. The study does not test model scaling, capability, or causal effects of training data/objectives on similarity.
record.rows_left_out: None. Sixty rows retained, the maximum allowed.

untested.parts: No size or capability progression, or relationship between improvement and alignment.
Only image embeddings are compared, including those of vision-language models; no paired image-caption alignment or improvement trend.
No controlled independent-initialization comparison of the same architecture.
No representation transfer, mapping, stitching or interchangeability performance test.
No identification of shared interpretable features or circuits.
No neighbour-count sweep or controlled distribution-shift comparison. TCGA was excluded from pretraining, but that alone does not measure weakening relative to training-distribution alignment.
No plateau over scale and no causal test establishing shared data or objectives as the explanation for alignment.

missing.what: Alternative-metric model averages: UNI2 0.527, Virchow2 0.383, Prov-GigaPath 0.578, CONCH 0.472, PLIP 0.481, KEEP 0.472. UNI2 ceases to be among the two lowest-average models.

Pairwise stain-normalization results, especially UNI2–natural-image DINOv2: 0.093 [0.030, 0.169] becomes 0.027 [−0.015, 0.122]. Aggregate rows conceal this reduction. Other pathology-pair means remain 0.286–0.571.
Direct robustness summaries: Pearson correlation between original and alternative similarity sets is 0.84 for distance metric and 0.997 for sampling.

Batch-level statistical comparisons of mean model similarity: UNI2 and Virchow2 are each below the other four pathology models, and Prov-GigaPath is above all five, with paired-test p < 0.05 for each stated comparison.

record.verdict_notes: All supplied numerical row values agree with the supplied text. The r1–r21 locator should identify Figure 2 as the original-patch matrix; Appendix Figure 5 uses normalized patches. States marked observed refer to V7's incomplete-alignment component; where V6 has a different state, that distinction is stated in the row's problem field. Positive but incomplete correlation supports V7 rather than constituting only partial observation of that challenge version. No verdict is assigned to untested scaling or causal components.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability scaling sweep; no test of whether alignment increases as models become larger or more capable.
No paired image-caption representation alignment test, and no scaling or performance comparison for vision and language models.
No independent training-seed comparison or shared-feature/subspace analysis.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired interchangeability test.
No analysis of recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits.

Tests Euclidean versus correlation-based RDM construction, stain-normalized versus original patches, and an alternative sampling configuration. Does not test out-of-distribution inputs or neighbour-count settings.

Measures model-to-model RDM similarity and compares training paradigms descriptively. Does not test a plateau over scale or establish whether shared data/objectives cause alignment rather than a common model of reality.
